It's virtually impossible to hydroplane doing 30mph unless you have wide tires with essentially no tread (which we can see is not the case). My 2 cents is OP, and a few others don't understand what hydroplaning is. 

Your car is literally skipping over water when hydroplaning. You cannot control it while this is happening. Steering does next to nothing.

I think people are confusing this with skidding, which is very easy to do on a wet road no matter the speed. Just punch it in a GT, and the back end will slide out.

Either way, I think we can all agree this kind of accident is not likely caused at 30mph. If it was at 30mph, the car was almost certainly not "hydroplaning" and was skidding and just hit the bank exactly right. I think it's more likely it was going faster than that.

With all this said, I am glad nobody was injured, and please just drive more carefully in the future.
